# Additional Resources for learning python

## General Data Analysis

<a href="https://wesmckinney.com/book/">Python for Data Analysis Open Edition</a> is a classic resource for data analysis (including data cleaning and data visualization). It's a great place to get started and also has a brief introduction to modeling libraries like <a href="https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/index.html">statsmodels</a> and <a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/">scikit-learn</a>. 

[*Python Rgonomics*](https://emilyriederer.netlify.app/post/py-rgo-2025/). An in-depth article on using tools in Python that are genuinely “Pythonic” while being consistent with the workflow and style of the best R has to offer (*we will cover some like `great_tables` and `plotnine` in later sessions. Stay tuned!*). 

## Data Science Tools

[**Official Positron Guide**](https://positron.posit.co/welcome.html). An all-Encompassing wikipedia of the Positron IDE with all tutorials you might need to get started with and learn more about the IDE. Some relevant guides

[***A Quick Tour of Positron***](https://posit.co/blog/a-quick-tour-of-positron/). To quickly learn how to navigate the Positron IDE.

[**Git and GitHub learning resources**](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/start-your-journey/git-and-github-learning-resources#using-git) by GitHub Docs with links to free online courses and tutorials.

## Machine Learning

<a href="https://scikit-learn.org/stable/">Scikit-learn</a> has some good tutorials and examples for machine learning and modeling on its official website. 

<a href="https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/basics/intro.html">PyTorch</a> also has an introductory tutorial and some other more in-depth tutorials including creating NLP models and visualizing models with TensorBoard. 

For hyperparameter tuning, <a href="github.com/optuna/optuna">optuna</a> and <a href="optuna-dashboard.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">optuna-dashboard</a> are pretty easy to use and work well with PyTorch.


## Using R and Python together

<a href="https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/">Reticulate</a> lets you run Python code from within R. <a href="https://rpy2.readthedocs.io/en/latest/">rpy2</a> lets you run R code from Python. If you install rpy2, you can use %%R to run R code in Jupyter notebooks with <a href="https://ipython.readthedocs.io/en/9.2.0/interactive/magics.html">Cell Magic commands</a>. 


## For working with large data

<a href="docs.pola.rs/user-guide/getting-started/">Polars</a> is an alternative to Pandas for working with large data (like datasets larger than available RAM). Not everything that works with Pandas will automatically work with Polars, but current versions of Scikit-learn have added support for it.
